reviews.text: The experience was highly disappointing. They say it’s a workout made by women for women and I ended up having videos of this male trainer that did not represent what I’m looking for. They market this product using the image of mature women who look fit and toned, but I received videos with a male trainer who, with all due respect, does not look fit and toned. So, which one is it? Can Tai Chi make your body fit and toned or not? Is not a good image to represent what they’re marketing. They use mature fit and toned women in the ads and the one who appeared to be “the face” of the product, is not in the videos. If you’re marketing a product with an image, that’s what you’re selling. You’re selling the image of a toned, fit mature female body that was reached by doing tai chi exercises. They promise quick changes in the ads, so awesome, that you should be “turning heads” by the 28th day. So, why did I get videos of this training “made by women for women” with a male trainer with a chubby appearance? I’m sorry for saying that, but it’s true. My goal is for real an I really needed what they marketed, but it was highly disappointing. Not only that, but if you are not satisfied by the end of the month, they say you may request a refund. reviews.title: Not recommended
reviews.text: Unfortunately I purchased a 1 year subscription to this app and have repeatedly been very disappointed. Got it for the Tai Chi but couldn’t complete past the 4th lesson as the instructions for the more advanced moves were very poor, confusing and too fast with no ability to review more slowly. Tried 2 different yoga programs that were very enjoyable but some of the instructions for positions were incorrect. When I emailed support they wanted screenshots and detailed descriptions which I don’t believe is my job. The classic yoga program also spontaneously disappeared from the library. Also the music randomly changes for no reason. Was also going to try the somatic yoga program with Marco, the male instructor but his reference to “men like you” was a little off putting for a woman. I have run out of good yoga programs in this app.

reviews.title: Beware of £49.99 after 28 days
reviews.text: The Tai-Chi for 28 days for £19.99 wasn’t bad. I found it wasn’t really my thing but was happy to try it. As some other people have said, it was confusing with left and right and looking at the instructor the opposite way round. Unfortunately, £49.99 was taken from my credit card with no obvious pre-warning. It was not very clear AT ALL that this would happen and that you need to cancel at least 24 hours before. I checked all my emails and could not find any mention of it anywhere until after the event. I was so cross that I contacted Yoga-GO to no avail so I then managed to get the money back from my credit card company. PLEASE PAY BY CREDIT CARD AND GET YOUR MONEY BACK IF YOU TO HAVE BEEN SCAMMED

reviews.title: Poor audio with constant static and choppy interval exercises
reviews.text:
App with great potential but poor audio and choppy interval exercises contribute to a an experience that does not match the price!  Audio has constant static which is very distracting when trying to do relaxing, focused tai chi. 
Variable time commitment per day: It also said the exercises were 14min per day but gradually day by day the length of time for the program increases.  You start at around 12min and by day 28 it’s 28min.  It would help if they explained this up front. 
The exercises are videoed to be longer programs but are edited and chopped into short segments based on your needs.  Great that it can be personalized, but it results in choppy segments that jump from one exercise without a good transition time. With the static-y audio it’s hard to ‘get into’ the exercise program and is not satisfying.

reviews.title: Misrepresented on Insta
reviews.text: I see that there are so many positive reviews for this app and that makes sense to me if your goal is to manage stress and relax.  However, I got the app and paid for three months of exercises based on wanting to get more toned and in shape, which several Instagram ads talked about and convinced me it would help with.  Those ads also said the daily practice that would be designed for me was  only seven minutes.  While the exercises are very calming and may create some tone in my arms, overall, there is no way they could possibly deliver what’s promised.  The workouts start at about 12 minutes a day and some days they are as many as 23 minutes, so definitely a different length than mentioned. Also almost half the workout ends up being meditation.  Again, this has its place and is very helpful in some ways, but it is not why I purchased it.  Personally, I also find the voice-over repetitive, unhelpful overtime, and grating.  Lastly, the camera work is unhelpful for following complicated Tai chi moves.  They zoom in and out making it hard to see the overall movement.

reviews.title: Careful - you will be on an auto-renewal
reviews.text:
Terrible scam-like auto renewal policy. I thought I had signed up for a single 30 day plan. Then they just took more money from me without any warning that it was going to happen. I cannot find anything in the app settings that makes clear this was going to happen.  
Edit: I have had a response from the developer. They say they do say it automatically reverses. They are missing my point that they do not make it stand out and they do not contact you shortly before the auto renewal point as a reminder. I am by no means the only person who fell foul of this, so I still think it is something they need to improve on.
